analysis.title: Take-Two Interactive Software Inc. (TTWO) FQ2'27 Earnings Review: FY27 Bookings Outlook Reiterated; Focus Remains Squarely on GTA VI Launch
key_insights: TTWO FQ2'27 net bookings of $1,601mm came in below GSe ($1,654mm) and consensus ($1,702mm), and below the company's $1,620-1,670mm guidance range, mainly because NBA 2K27 performed below internal expectations. It was still the second strongest launch in franchise history.

Management reiterated the FY27 net bookings outlook. GTA VI pre-orders are tracking well above initial expectations ahead of the November 19th release. Management is waiting for post-launch data before including any upside.

Recurrent consumer spend (RCS) fell 9% YoY in the quarter against management's expectation of a 5% decline. NBA 2K and mobile were both weak, including a double-digit % decline in Color Block Jam against a strong FQ2'26 comparison.

Mobile operating performance was relatively in line. Toon Blast and Words With Friends grew, advertising improved sequentially and the D2C channel continued to grow with a meaningful margin benefit per management.

FY27 GAAP revenue guidance rose modestly and FY27 operating expense guidance fell (+5% YoY), reflecting lower user-acquisition costs, partly from the timing of mobile releases. GTA VI marketing spend stays elevated and R&D is a growth driver.
GS expects the unchanged full-year outlook to imply confidence in GTA VI demand and an improvement in NBA 2K performance in 2H FY27, backed by the largest planned post-launch content slate.

GS lists the investor debates as: GTA VI launch-unit performance and Ultimate Edition mix, durability and cadence of GTA ecosystem engagement, the expected 2H acceleration in NBA 2K bookings, and mobile stabilization as Color Block Jam comps normalize.
GS reiterates Buy and raises its 12-month price target to $290 from $285. The price was $207.40, implying 39.8% upside.

GS cut FY27 non-GAAP EPS to $6.00 from $6.59 and non-GAAP EBIT to $1.41bn from $1.56bn. FY27 bookings stay at about $8.20bn. FQ3'27 bookings rise to $3.48bn from $2.70bn and FQ3 EPS to $3.43 from $3.11.
FY28 and FY29 estimates rise: FY28 EPS $8.70 (from $8.38) and FY29 EPS $10.91 (from $10.52). FY28 bookings are $8.70bn and FY29 bookings $9.42bn.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and raises the price target to $290 from $285 on updated estimates. GTA VI pre-orders are tracking well above expectations and the FY27 bookings outlook is unchanged despite an FQ2 bookings miss.

earnings_insights: TTWO FQ2'27 (reported 11/9): net bookings $1,601mm vs GSe $1,654mm, consensus $1,702mm, guidance $1,620-1,670mm. Net revenue $1,497mm vs GSe $1,456mm, consensus $1,460mm, guidance $1,420-1,470mm.
TTWO FQ2'27 non-GAAP EPS $0.99 reported vs GSe $0.97, consensus $0.97, guidance $0.90-1.00. Non-GAAP EBIT $230mm vs GSe $236mm, consensus $238mm.
TTWO FQ2'27 non-GAAP gross margin 69.1% vs GSe 69.7% and consensus 58.7%. Non-GAAP EBIT margin 14.3% vs GSe 14.2% and consensus 12.3%.
FQ2'27 RCS declined 9% YoY vs management's -5% expectation, reflecting weakness in NBA 2K and mobile.
GS FQ3'27E (GS estimates): net bookings $3.48bn (from $2.70bn), non-GAAP EBIT $801mm (from $729mm in Exhibit 2, $381mm in text), non-GAAP EPS $3.43 (from $3.11).
GS FY27E (GS estimates): net bookings $8.20bn, non-GAAP EBIT $1.41bn (from $1.56bn), non-GAAP EPS $6.00 (from $6.59). FY28E EPS $8.70 (from $8.38). FY29E EPS $10.91 (from $10.52).
GTA VI is scheduled for release on November 19th. Pre-orders are well above initial expectations, but management reiterated FY27 guidance pending post-launch data.
risk_factors: Engagement and user growth: lower units and live services sales for GTA, Red Dead Online and NBA 2K Online, or weaker reception of new games, and slower growth in mobile.
Integration: slower integration of acquisitions (namely Zynga), game release delays or core franchise decay could raise development spending.
Regulation: potential loss of licensing agreements for key IP and tighter regulation of loot boxes and microtransactions.
Competition: more competition in console and mobile as development tools commoditize, and consolidation among competitors.
Macro: weaker consumer spending and exposure to investor risk appetite for growth stocks.

key_data_points.context: Below GSe $1,654mm, consensus $1,702mm and guidance $1,620-1,670mm. Reported 11/9/2026.

key_data_points.anchor: ahead of the title’s November 19th release

tension_points.bull_case: GTA VI pre-orders are tracking well above initial expectations, GTA+ members and GTA series RCS rose, and management kept the FY27 bookings outlook unchanged. GS expects NBA 2K to improve in 2H FY27 on the largest planned post-launch content slate.
tension_points.bear_case: FQ2 bookings missed GSe and consensus and fell below guidance, RCS fell 9% YoY vs -5% expected, NBA 2K27 underperformed, and management is not raising guidance until it has post-launch data.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GTA VI launch-unit performance and Ultimate Edition mix after the November 19th release, and failure of NBA 2K bookings to accelerate in 2H FY27.

theme_stances.key_argument: The unchanged full-year outlook implies confidence in GTA VI demand and an improvement in NBA 2K performance in 2H27.
theme_stances.evidence: GTA VI pre-orders tracking well above initial expectations
